ety.text: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dāvàti. By surface analysis, дать (datʹ) + -ва́ть (-vátʹ). Cognate with Ukrainian дава́ти (daváty, “to give”), Belarusian дава́ць (davácʹ, “to give”), Bulgarian давам (davam, “I give”) (imperfective), Serbo-Croatian да́вати, dávati, Polish dawać (“to give”).
Perhaps from ди́во (dívo) + -и́ть (-ítʹ). Ultimately from Proto-Slavic *diviti.

ety.text: Borrowed from Ukrainian хло́пець (xlópecʹ, “boy, lad”), cognate to Polish chłopiec.

From хрю (xrju, “oink, sound of a pig”) + Украи́на (Ukraína). Russian jokes often stereotype Ukrainians as eating salo (salted pig fat); after the War in Donbas and the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine, in Russian nationalist discourse, this portrayal progressed to a dehumanizing association of enemy Ukrainian soldiers or Ukrainians in general with pigs (as opposed to merely pig-eaters).
